run.note_missing: 2026Q2 has no archived snapshot; 36 buckets cover 37 quarters

headline.metric: share of ticker-quarter observations that a naive ticker-keyed join attributes to the wrong CIK
headline.reported_as: 0.9% to 1.3% depending on where the clean window starts. Both endpoints are given because the choice of window is a judgement call, and hiding it behind one number would be the same sin the project is about.

strict.rationale: Starts after the post-contraction rebuild finished. Most conservative.

auto_selected.rationale: What EdgeSet.stable_window() picks: longest run with no single-quarter composition break above 25%. Includes the 2020Q3-2021Q3 rebuild, during which row count climbed 8,426 -> 12,837 gradually enough that no single quarter trips the threshold.

full_period.status: INFLATED. Do not quote without the caveat. Roughly a fifth of all detected transitions land on the two artifact snapshots.

ticker_change_cik_persists.note: same CIK, disjoint ticker spans - e.g. Ball Corporation BLL -> BALL in 2022Q3

share_class_and_multi_listing.caveat: mixed bucket - true share classes, preferred series, warrants, and bankruptcy Q-suffixed tickers are all in here. Not cleanly separated.

survivorship.status: NOT REPORTED AS A HEADLINE. Confounded by file composition changes; needs per-CIK filing-activity validation before it means anything.

artifacts_detected.description: Two snapshots where the SEC file's own composition changed, not the market. These generate false reuse and false delisting signals.

known_limitations: Gap collapsing: the edge builder extends a segment when a ticker reappears under the SAME CIK, so a delist-then-relist under one CIK is recorded as continuous. Measured effect: the segment-derived presence count exceeds the true file row count by 0 to 1,927 rows per snapshot. Reuse detection is unaffected; intra-period gaps are understated.
Transition dates are snapshot-resolution, not event-resolution. A change is dated to the first quarterly snapshot that shows it, which can lag the corporate event by years (see GOOGL).
This is SEC filer data, not a trading universe. No prices, no volumes, no exchange-level delisting records. Failure classes are real; market impact is inferred.
Wayback coverage starts 2017-08-28. Nothing before that.
The share-class bucket conflates share classes, preferreds, warrants and bankruptcy tickers. It is a count of concurrent multi-ticker CIKs, not a clean share-class count.

The submissions API's filings.recent block holds only the most recent ~1000 filings, so first-filing dates taken from it are wrong for high-volume filers. Full history requires filings.files. Life/death dating in this build does not rely on it.
